text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
The English Queen known as "Bloody Mary", MARY TUDOR, was born on this day in 1517. She earned the nickname through her relentless persecution of Protestants.
Spanish classical guitarist ANDRE SEGOVIA was born in 1893.

US accordionist, violinist, songwriter and bandleader PEE WEE KING (JULIUS FRANK KUCZYNSKI) was born in 1914. From 1947 to 1957, he had his own radio show and then, a TV show. IN 1948 he began to have success with his own songs such as "Tennessee Waltz".
American actor JACK PALANCE ("believe it ... or not") who later turned to comedy films like "CITY SLICKERS", was born in 1919.
Czech-born American film director MILOS FORMAN, ("ONE FLEW OVER THE CUCKOO'S NEST), was born in 1932.
YOKO ONO, wife of late "Beatle" JOHN LENNON, was born in 1934.
US country/pop singer JUICE NEWTON (JUDY KAY) was born in 1952. Her versions of "Angel Of The Morning" (1981) and "Queen Of Hearts" (1981) were both million sellers.

American singer RANDY CRAWFORD was born in 1952. She was initially more successful in the United Kingdom with ten hits there between 1979 and 1986. Her biggest hits were "One Day I'll Fly Away" (1980) and "Almaz" (1986).
Australian drummer with the original 'Little River Band' DEREK PELLICI was born in 1953.

American actor and dancer JOHN TRAVOLTA ("SATURDAY NIGHT FEVER", "GREASE", "LOOK WHO'S TALKING"), was born in 1955. His first success as an actor came with his part as "Vinnie Barbarino" in the television series "Welcome Back Kotter".
** EVENTS **
1564 : MICHELANGELO BUONAROTTI, whose greatest work was
arguably the "Book Of Genesis" on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, died in Rome at the age of 89.
1876 : The first direct telegraph link was established
between Britain and New Zealand.
1914 : A British exploration team claimed to have

discovered the ruins of three Inca cities in the Peruvian forests. Explorer Captain CAMPBELL BESLEY arrived in New York with tales of his journey. He said the buildings of the largest city were more impressive than London's Houses of Parliament. Two and a half years earlier the lost Inca capital of Machu Picchu was found near Cuzco by US historian Dr HIRAM BINGHAM.
1930 : The planet PLUTO was discovered by American
astronomer CLYDE TOMBAUGH. PLUTO was named after the Lord of Hades in Greek Mythology.
1933 : American prizefighter and world champion JAMES
"Gentleman Jim" CORBETT, died.
1946 : The Japanese ship "Koei Maru" arrived in Melbourne
to take home 2,100 POWs. No text received
1958 : The Australian Broadcasting Corporation televised
its first lessons for schools.
1958 : More than 200,000 people gave the Queen Mother an
uproariously informal welcome in Brisbane's humid weather.
1967 : The father of the A-Bomb, American physicist
ROBERT OPPENHEIMER, died.
1986 : South Africa's white government banned foreign
television crews from filming "disturbances" in black townships.
1990 : Demonstrators stormed the Headquarters of
Romania's provisional government, demanding the resignation of President ION ILESCU.
1991 : The American assault ship 'TRIPOLI' and
guided-missile cruiser 'PRINCETON' were damaged by mines while patrolling the Persian Gulf during the war with Iraq.
1992 : Libya handed over two men accused of bombing Pan
Am flight 103 over Lockerbie in Scotland, but refused to send them to stand trial in the West.
